newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq closes higher in post-election rally. [CORRECTED 22:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq closes higher in post-election rally. [CORRECTED 22:40 GMT]

text.p: High technology stocks, buoyed by President Bill Clinton's re-election, rallied and pushed the Nasdaq Composite Index to a sharply higher close.
Clinton, who will continue to work with a Republican-dominated Congress, is perceived as being positive for the high tech industry.
"He is talking about wiring schools to the internet," one analyst said. "There are other proposals that are designed to help the technologies as well."
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 16.4 points, or 1.33 percent, at 1245.5, while advances led declining issues by three to two on volume of about 635 million shares.

High tech shares were also driven by a strong earnings report from Cisco Systems Inc and the defeat of a California measure which could have threatened technology profits. Cisco was down 1/2 at 61-1/4 after running up in anticipation of the earnings which came after Tuesday's close. Intel Corp jumped 4-7/8 to 118-7/8 in active trading.
Oxford Health Plans Inc was up 4-5/8 at 51-1/2 after reporting third quarter earnings.
Intuit Inc rose seven to 36-1/2 on market rumors it would be taken over by American Express Co.
